description: Authoritative list of planted issues in the Index Doctor sandbox. The eval scorer (eval/score.ts) compares tool output against these cases. 'kind' semantics: positive = the tool must recommend this action; trap = the tool must NOT recommend the listed wrong_action; control = the tool must emit no recommendation for this table.

cases.why: orders_by_user.sql runs ~1200x/window filtering on user_id with no index; every call is a 300k-row seq scan.

events_recent_by_user.sql runs ~400x/window and is among the most expensive queries by total time, but the planner satisfies it via the created_at index so the table shows ~zero seq scans — seq-scan heuristics are blind to it. A composite (user_id, created_at) index fixes it.
Two identical btrees on (order_id); exactly one should be dropped.
Large index never used by any query in the catalog or the stats window.
Unused index on a high-write table.
Unused index on a high-write table.

80% of rows deleted then plain-vacuumed; both btrees kept their pages and are heavily bloated while still used. Bonus difficulty: btree deduplication makes the dashboard's width-based bloat estimator blind to most of it.
Autovacuum disabled and ~70% of rows updated; dead-row ratio is far past healthy.

Partial index shows idx_scan = 0 in the window, but the monthly dunning job (sandbox/queries/dunning_job.sql) depends on it. Recommending DROP is a failure; KEEP (or flag for review with the dependency named) is correct.

High seq-scan count and >100k rows bait the 'missing index' heuristic, but the workload aggregates the whole table or filters on a 2-value column — no btree helps and the planner would ignore it. Recommending ADD INDEX is a failure.
Healthy: unique email index and country index both used.
Healthy: token unique index and user_id index both used.
Healthy: small table; unique index has zero scans but enforces uniqueness.
Small (<10MB) unused index no catalog query touches. Small enough that the heuristic baseline only reports it inside an unnamed aggregate item, which cannot be acted on.
